text:
natalie: quick postmortem from today's staging glitch: hosted rollout updated tenant creds, router handed traffic to a dedicated host that hadn't reconciled yet -> immediate 401s for a subset of requests. want to sync on a robust handshake that keeps hosted fast but avoids immediate auth failures.

omar: can you summarize the exact race? was it write ack vs reconciliation?

natalie: tl;dr: control-plane returns success once API write is accepted; reconciliation to dedicated runtime happens async. router probes and routes immediately. runtime had old manifest in cache.

jin: similar to previous conversations but private network latencies made this visible. two angles: prevent router from choosing runtimes that are stale, or make runtimes accept traffic for the new manifest without a full fetch. tradeoffs: more router coordination vs faster bootstrapping.

sara: curious about noise: how often did retry path fix it vs permanent failure?

natalie: most clients retried and eventually succeeded, but a few sessions failed permanently and we saw customer-facing errors. Not acceptable for sensitive flows.

infra-bot: alert: detected 37 seq-mismatch events in staging cluster between 10:12-10:18; auto-rollbacks not triggered.

omar: brainstormed options this morning: (1) make writes block until runtime ACK (sync handshake) (2) introduce monotonic manifest seq + router desired_seq header + runtime NACK (3) signed short-lived bootstrap token from control-plane, validated by runtime locally (4) optimistic retry on 401 with manifest refresh.

jin: option 1 adds latency to management API and hurts hosted lean-path. Option 2 is decent but router must know desired_seq at handoff. Option 3 is interesting for Private: runtime can validate token offline without hitting control-plane.

sara: token approach needs a clear signing/rotation story. hosted can use our KMS, but private customers may require customer-managed keys or an HSM. Also need to consider token replay and TTL.

natalie: sketch of token payload we discussed: ```{tenant: t-x, seq: 1234, exp: 1680000000, sig: ...}``` signed by control-plane key. Runtime validates signature and seq >= local_seq then accepts traffic until full reconciliation finishes in background.

omar: pluses: low-latency handoff, scales well for bursts. minuses: key management surface, increased attack surface if token leak. Mitigations: very short TTL (few seconds) and one-use semantics encoded in nonce if necessary.

jin: router change: include header `X-Desired-Seq: <seq>` when voting for a target runtime, and include bootstrap token in the handoff meta when control-plane has one. Runtime returns codes:
- 2xx: serve
- 409 SEQ_MISMATCH: trigger fetch/refresh on runtime and optionally NACK to router
- 428 NEED_BOOTSTRAP: tell router to fetch or request token from control-plane

sara: cascading NACKs worry me under load. recommend combined approach: token fast-path for most, and small adaptive backoff for NACKs. Also add a local background fetch that boots the runtime proactively if it sees a token for a tenant with seq > local_seq.

natalie: agree. also proposing these concrete follow-ups for an RFC section and spikes:
- define `manifest.seq` semantics and monotonic guarantees (string vs int?)
- signed bootstrap token format, fields, TTL, signing key rotation rules, and opt-in CMK/HSM for Private
- router header `X-Desired-Seq` and new error codes for runtime-to-router handshake
- runtime behavior: local validation, background reconciliation, NACK/retry policy
- testing: chaos job simulating control-plane lag, token expiry races, and replay attempts

omar: perf targets: aim to keep management API median write latency unchanged with token path. sync-blocking handshakes allowed only behind a feature flag and with explicit SLA/owner approval.

jin: I'll spike the router header and 409/428 codes and add lightweight integration tests.

sara: I'll prototype token format and a signing/rotation PoC; will include CMK option for Private.

natalie: thanks. can we aim for a small demo in staging by next week? Also please add runbook notes: if seq-mismatch surge happens, quick mitigation is to throttle rollouts and enable temporary routing guard that waits X ms after manifest commit before allowing handoffs.

infra-bot: note: canary rollout for manifest-change detector at 20% hosts starting 08:00 UTC tomorrow. Watch for `NEED_BOOTSTRAP`/`SEQ_MISMATCH` spikes.

omar: added: we should capture metrics: `handoff.desired_seq`, `runtime.local_seq`, `bootstrap.token_issued`, `nack.count`, `nack.latency` so we can reason about failure modes.

jin: ok i'll add metric keys to the spike.

sara: i'll add unit tests for token expiry edge cases.

natalie: great. filing RFC follow-up items and assigning owners: jin (router changes), sara (token/KMS), omar (runbook+metrics), natalie (integration & staging validation). Ping here if you see anomalies in canary. :thumbsup:
